blocks.content: Compose's volumes section is a declarative wrapper around the same named volumes covered in the Docker Volumes module, declared once, referenced by any service that needs to persist data.
1. Declaring a Volume Once, at the Top Level
blocks.text: 1. Declaring a Volume Once, at the Top Level

blocks.content: A named volume a service needs is declared once under the top-level volumes key, this is Compose's equivalent of running docker volume create yourself, Compose handles the creation automatically the first time it is needed.

blocks.alt: Declared once, at the top of the file

blocks.content: A service mounts that named volume by referencing it in its own volumes list, exactly the same name:path shape as a plain docker run -v flag, just expressed declaratively.

blocks.alt: A service references the volume by the name declared above

blocks.content:
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    volumes:
      - dbdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
volumes:
  dbdata:

code.content:

codes.yaml:
services:

  dbdata:

blocks.content: This distinction matters in practice: plain docker compose down stops and removes containers, but leaves named volumes, and their data, intact. Only docker compose down -v additionally removes those volumes, a deliberate, separate decision, not an accident.

blocks.alt: Data survives a plain down, only -v removes it too

blocks.content:
docker compose down       # containers gone, dbdata volume and its data remain
docker compose down -v    # containers AND dbdata volume are both removed

code.content:
docker compose down       # containers gone, dbdata volume and its data remain
docker compose down -v    # containers AND dbdata volume are both removed

codes.bash:
docker compose down       # containers gone, dbdata volume and its data remain
docker compose down -v    # containers AND dbdata volume are both removed

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Compose volumes are declared once at the top level and referenced by name from any service, the same named-volume model from the Docker Volumes module.
A plain docker compose down keeps volume data intact, only the explicit -v flag removes volumes along with the containers.
